traps: Median nerve: cutaneous branch but NO autonomous zone.
Cranial circumflex humeral = axillary branch; caudal circumflex humeral = subscapular branch.
Axillary → brachial after cranial circumflex humeral; brachial → median after common interosseous.
Superficial paw = COMMON DIGITAL; deep paw = METACARPAL. Prefix dorsal/palmar by surface.
Cephalic drains MEDIAL; accessory cephalic drains DORSAL and LATERAL.
External thoracic → superficial pectorals; lateral thoracic → deep pectoral.
Cranial pectoral nerve → superficial pectorals; caudal pectoral nerve → deep pectoral.
No terminal lymph node for thoracic limb; head = medial retropharyngeal; pelvic limb has one.
Axillary lymph node = constant; accessory axillary = inconstant, drains INTO axillary.
Superficial cervical node drains limb EXCEPT medial arm, forearm, shoulder.
Brachial plexus = VENTRAL branches C6–T2; dorsal branches go epaxial.
Deep digital flexor is dual: median AND ulnar nerves.
Radial nerve autonomous zone stops at lateral half of digit 5 — that's ulnar.
flags: Functional-loss answers derive muscle actions from prior muscle lectures/standard anatomy, not L19 sources. Confirm against the OIA document.
Blueprint says 'four major superficial veins' but the slide lists five (cephalic, accessory cephalic, median cubital, axillobrachial, omobrachial). Ask which four.
Deep antebrachial and radial arteries: slides place them off the median artery; transcript 'it' is ambiguous. Using slides.
Median vs ulnar to deep digital flexor: transcript says 'median nerve, sometimes it does, sometimes it does not' — unclear what varies. Ask.
Superficial cervical node location: slide says covered by brachiocephalicus AND omotransversarius; transcript says deep to omotransversarius only. Not contradictory; use slide.
Ulnar 'two testing sites': transcript garbles it as two branches of caudal cutaneous antebrachial nerve; slide shows caudal cutaneous antebrachial + palmar branch. Using slide.
Autonomous zone map is an image not captured in slide text; zone locations are from transcript wording only.
Radial artery branches: transcript says dorsal and palmar branch; slides label dorsal carpal branch and palmar branch.
